name: Inverse rule
summary: The scalar √2 (a Z- and X-spider joined by one wire) is inverse to a Z- and X-spider joined by three wires.
description:
A Z-spider and an X-spider connected by a single wire represent the scalar $\sqrt2$, and a Z-spider and an X-spider connected by three wires represent $\frac1{\sqrt2}$. Together they are the empty diagram, i.e. the scalar 1.

Backens, Perdrix and Wang introduced this rule to replace the 'star' generator (a new node representing the scalar $\frac12$) and the star rule that Backens had used to make the stabilizer ZX-calculus complete for scalars: every non-zero stabilizer scalar can then be inverted using diagrams built from spiders only.
notes: The right-hand side is the empty diagram.
